kind: historical recorded measurements, not a new benchmark
source: historical paper-figure facts, aggregate transcription; original timing script not recovered

original_protocol.server: streamlit run app.py on 127.0.0.1:8766, headless, fileWatcherType none; DB_PATH/DATA_DIR pointed at a scratch copy of the app DB (sqlite3 backup from an immutable read-only connection); dashboard inputs under exports/ read in place, read-only
original_protocol.browser: Playwright 1.61.0 bundled Chromium 149.0.7827.55, headless; viewport 1440x900, device_scale_factor 1 for timing; service workers blocked; only 127.0.0.1/localhost requests allowed
original_protocol.url: / (default landing page = Dashboard BI, normal mode, not print mode)
original_protocol.cold_load_definition: navigation start (performance.timeOrigin) to the first animation frame where the app script state is 'notRunning', the KPI row shows 5 metrics, >=3 visible Vega-Lite charts all contain svg.marks, the visible KPI sparkline is drawn and no spinner is visible
original_protocol.cold_load_runs: one warm-up load (first page load after server start; fills the Streamlit data cache), then 5 loads, each in a fresh browser context (empty browser cache and new Streamlit session) in the same browser process
original_protocol.warm_rerun_definition: in a further fresh context after load: programmatic click on the 'Airbnb' source pill (filter toggled on/off alternately, 5 changes); time from click to the end of the script run with every visible Vega-Lite chart redrawn (new svg element); change 1 was the first visit of the 'Airbnb only' filter state
original_protocol.measurement_conditions: the development machine with other user applications running (IDE, messaging apps and an unrelated GPU model-evaluation process); system CPU load (Win32_Processor.LoadPercentage) sampled 40-62% just before the timing run; not an isolated benchmark machine

conditions.server_cache: filled by the first-after-server-start navigation; warm during all five fresh-browser-context observations
conditions.machine: shared development laptop; background applications running
